extracted.intended_audience: PR practitioners, brand marketers, communications professionals
extracted.subtask_description: A short-form post-mortem analyzing a brand advertising misstep and extracting lessons for PR and marketing teams about messaging, creative process, and crisis response when campaigns intersect with social issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Authenticity matters. Brands can’t parachute into emotionally charged territory, use protest imagery as a prop, and expect praise for being “in touch.” The audience is quick to sense when something feels performative or opportunistic — and they’ll call it out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before engaging with social movements, evaluate whether the brand's involvement is genuine and grounded in values and actions. Avoid using imagery or narratives that trivialize real struggles. If the connection feels forced, the risk of backlash often outweighs the reward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid trivializing or co-opting social movements
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics noted how the ad suggested that a can of soda could resolve systemic issues, undermining the real stakes behind actual protests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not depict a product or brand action as a simplistic solution to systemic problems. Respect the context and stakes of movements; consult representatives or stakeholders to ensure portrayal is not demeaning, reductive, or exploitative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test messaging with external perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative work needs friction. One of the biggest red flags in post-mortem coverage was that the ad was developed in-house with minimal external pushback. Especially when addressing sensitive themes, it’s critical to test messaging with people outside the brand bubble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include diverse external reviewers, consultants, or community voices in concept and script reviews. Use focus groups or advisory panels that represent affected communities to surface tone-deafness before public launch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative development should avoid echo chambers
rubrics_metrics.description: Great ideas rarely come from echo chambers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design creative processes to solicit dissenting views and challenge assumptions. Encourage internal critique and bring in independent creative or cultural consultants to counter groupthink.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess brand-issue fit before weighing in
rubrics_metrics.description: Brands don’t need to weigh in on every cultural issue. When the connection between brand and message feels forced, the risk of backlash often outweighs the reward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform an explicit fit assessment: is there a genuine, defensible link between the brand and the social issue? If not, refrain from opportunistic commentary or campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate reputational vs financial risk
rubrics_metrics.description: While the ad didn’t cause a financial collapse like other PR crises, the reputational damage was significant. It sparked deep discussions around corporate activism, tone, and the risks of brands inserting themselves into sensitive cultural conversations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model both short‑term and long‑term reputational impacts (public sentiment, media narratives, stakeholder trust) alongside direct financial exposure when deciding on campaign strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis response must include depth and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: There’s also a lesson in crisis response. While Pepsi acted quickly in pulling the ad, its apology lacked depth. “We missed the mark” doesn’t explain how or why, and it didn’t lay out steps the company would take to do better.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When apologizing, clearly acknowledge specific harms, explain what went wrong, and provide concrete corrective actions and timelines. Audiences expect transparency and commitments to structural change, not perfunctory statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and posture of response — know when to speak or stay silent
rubrics_metrics.description: Pepsi went quiet for a while after the incident. There was no defensive press tour or spin campaign. Instead, the company regrouped and focused on safer, more conventional marketing in the months that followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether immediate engagement, sustained dialogue, or a temporary pause is the best posture. Consider stakeholder expectations, the nature of the harm, and whether additional communication will help or inflame the situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution, context, and humility over intention
rubrics_metrics.description: Good intentions aren’t enough. Execution, context, and humility matter — especially when the stakes are high and the audience is watching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize careful execution and contextual awareness; acknowledge limitations and avoid confident claims about understanding complex social issues. Approach sensitive topics with humility and deference to affected communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn from post-mortems to inform future strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pepsi ad backlash remains a cautionary tale for how not to engage with social issues in marketing... It sparked deep discussions around corporate activism, tone, and the risks of brands inserting themselves into sensitive cultural conversations without proper context or understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document lessons, update internal guidelines, and implement process changes (e.g., mandatory cultural competency reviews) so similar missteps are less likely in future campaigns.
